notes.meaning: David calls on the angels in heaven to honor God and declare His power. Even the highest spiritual beings must bow before the Lord and praise His greatness. This reminds us that all real strength belongs to God alone.

Worshippers are told to give the Lord the praise that matches His holy character. They are called to bow before Him with reverence and clean hearts, dressed in the beauty of holiness. True worship honors God for His absolute purity and goodness.

The thunder rolling across the rain clouds reveals the magnificent voice of the Lord. God demonstrates His glory by commanding the heavy storm clouds and vast waters above. Hearing the thunder prompts people to stand in awe of their Creator.

The voice of the Lord rings out with raw power and royal splendor. A booming tempest proves that nothing in the created world can match His authority. His word carries supreme majesty over all things.

Lightning and thunder crash through the mountain forests, shattering the giant cedars of Lebanon. These tall trees were known for being nearly indestructible, yet the storm snaps them easily. Human pride and worldly strength are completely helpless before God.

The massive mountains of Lebanon and Sirion seem to leap like startled calves or wild oxen under the fury of the storm. Fierce winds and shaking ground make the solid hills appear to tremble and jump. Even the grandest peaks on earth must bend to the Lord's presence.

God speaks, and brilliant flashes of lightning cut through the dark sky like blazing flames. His command sends fiery bolts shooting down across the land. Every sudden flash shows how swiftly and sharply His power works in creation.

The fierce storm travels south and shakes the great, barren desert of Kadesh. Even in lonely and dry wastelands where few people live, the Lord makes His presence felt. His mighty voice echoes across the entire land from north to south.

The roaring tempest strips the leaves off forest trees and frightens the wild deer into giving birth early. While nature trembles outside in fear, God's people assemble safely inside His sanctuary. There, worshippers look at His mighty deeds and joyfully shout, 'Glory!'

The Lord sits enthroned over the raging floodwaters, controlling the storm just as He ruled over Noah's great flood. No violent surge of water can ever threaten His eternal rule. He remains the sovereign King who keeps the whole world in order.

The same almighty Lord who rules the terrifying storm uses His strength to defend His own people. He grants them endurance in tough times and surrounds them with lasting peace. Believers can rest calmly knowing that their strong King watches over them.
